body:
Applicable behaviour: the pinned @ordarium 1.3.x "ORD-BOOT-0" commit-observation cursor semantics — a durable, opaque, filter-independent global change position that is always returned and that fails closed (INVALID_CURSOR) when it is not a valid durable position.

Evidence that this workspace's integration is 1.3.1, not 1.2.0:
- package.json lines 32-37 pin all four @ordarium packages to .../ordarium-v1.3.1/*.tgz; pnpm-workspace.yaml overrides repeat the same four URLs.
- Installed artifacts agree: node_modules/@ordarium/core/package.json, .../ledger-sqlite/package.json, .../host-kit/package.json all report "version": "1.3.1" (no 1.2.0 string anywhere under node_modules/@ordarium). No pnpm-lock.yaml exists in this snapshot, so the verifiable layers are pin == overrides == installed.

Behaviour actually in force at 1.3.1 (from the pinned artifacts):
- Capability-gated existence: SqliteLedger declares capabilities.stateChangeFeed=true and implements changes(); StateStore.changes() is guarded by supportsStateChangeFeed (capability flag AND a changes function), else LEDGER_CAPABILITY_REQUIRED. This is the "incremental observation of committed state revisions after a durable position".
- Cursor shape/semantics: opaque base64url of {"c":"<digits>"}, a global database change_seq; filter (namespace/limit) never changes its meaning. StateChangePage.cursor is always present (unlike the nextCursor? pagination of other read surfaces), so a consumer at the end of the feed still holds a resume position; hasMore flags further matching changes; order is ascending.
- Fail-closed invalidation: decodeStateChangeCursor throws InvalidCursorError (INVALID_CURSOR, "refusing to guess a resume point") for malformed/foreign cursors instead of restarting from the beginning; and changes() re-checks the decoded position against the ledger's global high-water mark — a restored/replaced ledger lowers the mark, so after > high-water throws INVALID_CURSOR. Concurrent commits only raise the mark, so valid cursors are never falsely rejected.
- Atomicity/migration: the ordarium_state_changes ordering row is inserted in the same transaction as the state revision, so a committed revision and its observable position are never split; LEDGER_SCHEMA_VERSION is 4 and the v3->v4 migration backfills synthetic positions in (namespace,key,revision) order, explicitly labelled migration order (not original commit order), after which new commits carry the real durable order.

Why the 1.2.0 description does NOT apply: docs/release-commentary-1.2.0.md self-scopes ("This commentary describes the state at the 1.2.0 release line: it predates the incremental state-change feed, so it has no notion of a change-feed cursor and no cursor-invalidation failure. Anything here applies only to the 1.2.0 line"; status historical/superseded). That is explicit version scope plus explicit supersession, so it is not co-applicable to this workspace. The workspace's own engineering records still saying 1.2.0 (docs/engineering/07-ordarium-alignment.md r1-r19, 03-system-design-spec.md baseline line, docker/minimal/README.md, CURRENT-STATE-ASSESSMENT.md) are stale paperwork relative to the dependency manifest; they describe an earlier pin, not the resolved integration.

Scope note: palimpsest's current Ordarium state path (src/telemetry/state_persistence.ts, TelemetryStateSync) consumes the state kind via list() pagination + write() CAS and never calls changes(); no .changes( call exists in src/. So the observation cursor is offered by the pinned line but not exercised by palimpsest code; where it is used, the 1.3.1 semantics above govern.

No peer contact needed: the apparent conflict is a version-scope/supersession question that the local dependency manifest and the pinned artifacts settle deterministically; nothing load-bearing remains unresolved for ordarium.main to supply.
